chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Umar ibn Aslam, who said:

The cupper performed cupping on me and shaved from the site of the fovea (the puncture mark). So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saw me and said: 'What is this? Go and shave your head.' He said: 'So I went and shaved my head.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan, referring to Imam Ali al-Rida (peace be upon him)
key_terms.النُّقْرَةِ: The puncture or small hole made during cupping (hijama)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida (as) say when he saw someone with shaved hair at the cupping site?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) observes a man whose cupping practitioner had shaved only the specific puncture site (*nuqrah*), and instructs him to shave his entire head. This incident highlights the scholarly discussion on whether partial shaving suffices for ritual purity or if complete shaving is preferred to remove any residual impurity or hair associated with the procedure, reflecting the meticulous attention to physical cleanliness (*taharah*) in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Umar Bin Aslam who said,

‘The cupper performed cupping on me in the fovea, so Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saw me, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Which thing is this? Go and shave-off your head!’ He (the narrator) said, ‘So I went and shaved-off my head’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Umar ibn Aslam who has said the following:
“I once applied cupping. The cupping man shaved that area. Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saw me and asked, ‘What is this? Go and shave your head.’ I went and shaved my head.’”
